content: Copper alloys are materials in which copper serves as the primary component. These alloys are known for their exceptional resistance to corrosion. Pure electrolytic copper, due to its superior electrical conductivity, is predominantly utilized in the production of electrical cables. The external appearance of various copper alloys can be quite similar, which, combined with the diverse combinations of elements used in their creation, can make it challenging to categorize them accurately. There are approximately 400 different compositions of copper and copper alloys, which are broadly classified into categories such as copper, high-copper alloys, brasses, bronzes, copper-nickels, copper–nickel–zinc (commonly referred to as nickel silver), leaded copper, and special alloys. Below are some of the principal alloying elements and their corresponding alloy types. Brasses Brass is an alloy composed of copper and zinc. Typically, brasses exhibit a yellow coloration. The zinc content in brass can range from a few percent to approximately 40%. However, as long as the zinc content remains below 15%, the corrosion resistance of copper is not significantly diminished. Under certain conditions, brasses can be susceptible to a type of selective leaching corrosion known as dezincification, where zinc is leached out of the alloy, leaving behind a porous copper structure. Bronzes Bronze is an alloy of copper combined with other metals, most commonly tin, but also aluminum and silicon. Aluminum bronzes are alloys of copper and aluminum, with aluminum content typically ranging between 5% and 11%. Additional elements such as iron, nickel, manganese, and silicon are sometimes included. Aluminum bronzes exhibit greater strength and corrosion resistance compared to other types of bronzes, particularly in marine environments. They also demonstrate low reactivity to sulfur compounds. The aluminum in these alloys forms a thin passivation layer on the metal's surface, enhancing its durability. Precious Metal Alloys Copper is frequently alloyed with precious metals such as silver and gold to create specialized alloys. Examples include Corinthian bronze, hepatizon, tumbaga, and shakudo. These alloys often possess unique aesthetic and functional properties, making them valuable in various applications.
